arxiv-1605-02269.title: Predicting Performance on MOOC Assessments using Multi-Regression Models
arxiv-1605-02269.creator: Zhiyun Ren Huzefa Rangwala Aditya Johri
arxiv-1605-02269.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Zhiyun Ren Huzefa Rangwala Aditya Johri. The past few years has seen the rapid growth of data mining approaches for the analysis of data obtained from Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs). The objectives of this study are to develop approaches to predict the scores a student may achieve on a given grade-related assessment based on information, considered as prior performance or prior activity in the course.

arxiv-2303-16510.title: Infeasible Deterministic, Stochastic, and Variance-Reduction Algorithms for Optimization under Orthogonality Constraints
arxiv-2303-16510.creator:
ame Pierre Ablin \email pierre.ablin@apple.com, 
ame Simon Vary \email simon.vary@uclouvain.be, 
ame Bin Gao \email gaobin@lsec.cc.ac.cn, 
ame P.-A. Absil \email pa.absil@uclouvain.be
arxiv-2303-16510.description: Abstract Orthogonality constraints naturally appear in many machine learning problems, from principal component analysis to robust neural network training. They are usually solved using Riemannian optimization algorithms, which minimize the objective function while enforcing the constraint. However, enforcing the orthogonality constraint can be the most time-consuming operation in such algorithms.

arxiv-2307-12925.title: The phase transition for the Gaussian free field is sharp
arxiv-2307-12925.creator: Pete Rigas
arxiv-2307-12925.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Pete Rigas. We prove that the phase transition for the Gaussian free field (GFF) is sharp. In comparison to a previous argument due to Rodriguez in 2017 which characterized a 0 − 1 0-1 law for the Massive Gaussian Free Field by analyzing crossing probabilities below a threshold h ∗ ⁣ ∗ h_{**} , we implement a strategy due to Duminil-Copin and Manolescu in 2016, which establishes that two parameters are equal, one of which encapsulates the probability of obtaining an infinite connected component

arxiv-2502-15149.title: Boundary-Driven Complex Brillouin Zone in Non-Hermitian Electric Circuits
arxiv-2502-15149.creator: Yung Kim, Sonu Verma, Minwook Kyung, Kyungmin Lee, Wenwen Liu, Shuang Zhang, Bumki Min, Moon Jip Park
arxiv-2502-15149.description: Abstract Complex-valued physical quantities, often non-conserved, represent key phenomena in non-Hermitian systems such as dissipation and localization. Recent advancements in non-Hermitian physics have revealed boundary-condition-sensitive band structures, characterized by a continuous manifold of complex-valued momentum known as the generalized Brillouin zone (GBZ). However, the ability to actively manipulate the GBZ and its associated topological properties has remained largely unexplored.

arxiv-2503-03965.title: All-atom Diffusion Transformers: Unified generative modelling of molecules and materials
arxiv-2503-03965.creator: Chaitanya K. Joshi, Xiang Fu, Yi-Lun Liao, Vahe Gharakhanyan, Benjamin Kurt Miller, Anuroop Sriram, Zachary W. Ulissi
arxiv-2503-03965.description: Abstract Diffusion models are the standard toolkit for generative modelling of 3D atomic systems. However, for different types of atomic systems – such as molecules and materials – the generative processes are usually highly specific to the target system despite the underlying physics being the same.

arxiv-2503-14374.title: Cross-Validation in Penalized Linear Mixed Models: Addressing Common Implementation Pitfalls
arxiv-2503-14374.creator: Tabitha K. Peter, Patrick J. Breheny
arxiv-2503-14374.description: Abstract In this paper, we develop an implementation of cross-validation for penalized linear mixed models. While these models have been proposed for correlated high-dimensional data, the current literature implicitly assumes that tuning parameter selection procedures developed for independent data will also work well in this context.

arxiv-2506-08297.title: SEMA: a Scalable and Efficient Mamba like Attention via Token Localization and Averaging Thanks: Qualcomm AI Research is an initiative of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
arxiv-2506-08297.creator: Nhat Thanh Tran, Fanghui Xue, Shuai Zhang, Jiancheng Lyu, Yunling Zheng, Yingyong Qi, Jack Xin
arxiv-2506-08297.description: Abstract Attention is the critical component of a transformer. Yet the quadratic computational complexity of vanilla full attention in the input size and the inability of its linear attention variant to focus have been challenges for computer vision tasks. We provide a mathematical definition of generalized attention and formulate both vanilla softmax attention and linear attention within the general framework.

arxiv-2508-07786.title: Proof-theoretic Semantics for Second-order Logic Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes: 03F05, 03B15, 03F03
arxiv-2508-07786.creator: Alexander V. Gheorghiu, David J. Pym
arxiv-2508-07786.description: Abstract . We develop a proof-theoretic semantics (P-tS) for second-order logic (S-oL), providing an inferentialist alternative to both full and Henkin model-theoretic interpretations. Our approach is grounded in base-extension semantics (B-eS), a framework in which meaning is determined by inferential roles relative to atomic systems — collections of rules that encode an agent’s pre-logical inferential commitments.

arxiv-2512-10585.title: Is Dark Energy Dynamical in the DESI Era? A Critical Review
arxiv-2512-10585.creator: Salvatore Capozziello, Himanshu Chaudhary, Tiberiu Harko, G. Mustafa
arxiv-2512-10585.description: Abstract We investigate whether the recent DESI DR2 measurements provide or not evidences for dynamical dark energy by exploring the ω 0 ​ ω a \omega_{0}\omega_{a} CDM model and its extensions with free ∑ m ν \sum m_{\nu} and N eff N_{\mathrm{eff}} .

arxiv-2512-18080.title: From Prompt to Product: A Human-Centered Benchmark of Agentic App Generation Systems
arxiv-2512-18080.creator: Marcos Ortiz, Justin Hill, Collin Overbay, Ingrida Semenec, Frederic Sauve-Hoover, Jim Schwoebel, Joel Shor
arxiv-2512-18080.description: Abstract Agentic AI systems capable of generating full-stack web applications from natural language prompts (“prompt-to-app”) represent a significant shift in software development. However, evaluating these systems remains challenging, as visual polish, functional correctness, and user trust are often misaligned. As a result, it is unclear how existing prompt-to-app tools compare under realistic, human-centered evaluation criteria.

pmc-10569322.title: Trishul division of mental health: Conveying all sadness or stress of life is NOT a mental illness to people, the public, professionals, and policymakers
pmc-10569322.creator: Narayana Manjunatha
pmc-10569322.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This could be a reason for over-medicalizing/over-psychiatrization for the presence of psychosocial stressors as a mental illness in scientific literature. The false concept of mental illness among people, the public, professionals, and policymakers

I come across people who call themselves mentally ill, even when they are perfectly normal, stating that “I am depressed/anxious,” especially after the famous Bollywood stars confessed to having mental illness.

pmc-10649923.title: The Impact of Structural Variations and Coating Techniques on the Microwave Properties of Woven Fabrics Coated with PEDOT:PSS Composition
pmc-10649923.creator: Vitalija Rubežienė, Sandra Varnaitė-Žuravliova, Audronė Sankauskaitė, Julija Pupeikė, Paulius Ragulis, Aušra Abraitienė, Lei Wang
pmc-10649923.description: Minimizing the impact of electromagnetic radiation (EMR) holds paramount importance in safeguarding individuals who frequently utilize electrical and electronic devices. Electrically conductive textiles, which possess specialized EMR shielding features, present a promising solution to mitigate the risks related to EMR.

pmc-11378961.title: Quantitative analysis of loxoprofen sodium loaded microspheres comprising pectin and its thiolated conjugates: In-vivo evaluation of their sustained release behavior
pmc-11378961.creator: Aisha Anam, Ghulam Abbas, Shahid Shah, Malik Saadullah, Dure Shahwar, Khalid Mahmood, Muhammad Hanif, Nabeel Ahmad, Ejaz Basheer, Ahmad J. Obaidullah, Hadil Faris Alotaibi, Mohammed Alqarni, Nabeela Ameer
pmc-11378961.description: Continuous use of oral NSAIDs can damage mucosal membrane, which results in decreased bioavailability and non-compliance with the therapy. But the use of sustained release drug delivery systems might offer a solution. Objective was to synthesize mucoadhesive SR microspheres by using different combinations of pectin (PEC) and its thiolated derivative (T-PEC3100) for improved loxoprofen (LS) permeation.

pmc-11713971.title: Unleashing the power of a willow bark‐derived tannin to alleviate behavioral deficits in a preclinical model of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11713971.creator: Ezaldean A Kahil, Anisha Jackson, Kruti Patel, Lori A Coward, Bernadette D'Souza, Gregory Gorman, Patricia Jumbo‐Lucioni
pmc-11713971.description: BackgroundDespite some advances in treatment, a cure for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains elusive. Disease hallmarks include heightened neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, associated with progressive decline in mobility and cognitive functions. Natural compounds provide a valuable reservoir of novel bioactive substances with therapeutic potential, fewer side effects, and increased affordability.

pmc-12523902.title: Emerging Radioligands as Tools to Track Multi-Organ Senescence
pmc-12523902.creator: Anna Gagliardi, Silvia Migliari, Alessandra Guercio, Giorgio Baldari, Tiziano Graziani, Veronica Cervati, Livia Ruffini, Maura Scarlattei, Alessio Imperiale
pmc-12523902.description: Senescence is a dynamic, multifaceted process implicated in tissue aging, organ dysfunction, and intricately associated with numerous chronic diseases. As senescent cells accumulate, they drive inflammation, fibrosis, and metabolic disruption through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Despite its clinical relevance, senescence remains challenging to detect non-invasively due to its heterogeneous nature and the lack of universal biomarkers.

pmc-12634936.title: Opioid Use among People with Migraine: Results of the OVERCOME (US) Study
pmc-12634936.creator: Sait Ashina, Elizabeth Johnston, E Jolanda Muenzel, Gilwan Kim, Dawn C Buse, Michael L Reed, Robert E Shapiro, Susan Hutchinson, Anthony J Zagar, Robert A Nicholson, Richard B Lipton
pmc-12634936.description: IntroductionDespite expert recommendations against using opioids for migraine treatment, their use remains common in the USA. We aimed to evaluate the use of opioids among people with active migraine using data from the Observational Survey of the Epidemiology, Treatment, and Care of Migraine (OVERCOME) (US) study.

pmc-13276135.title: Displaced minds: ecologies of depression
pmc-13276135.creator: Aila Akosua Kattner
pmc-13276135.description: This issue of the Biomedical Journal explores emerging perspectives across neuropsychiatry, metabolism, aging, regenerative medicine, artificial intelligence, and chronic inflammatory disease. Featured contributions examine epigenetic and neuroendocrine mechanisms in depression, including the antidepressant-like effects of magnolol in chronic stress-induced models and the potential relevance of short-chain fatty acids as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in major depressive disorder.

pmc-13385174.title: Alterations in submaximal cardiopulmonary indicators in CVD patients participating in APBCRE—a comprehensive CPET-based study
pmc-13385174.creator: Yukun Liang, Mei Ma
pmc-13385174.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of a one-month Adaptive Postural Balance Cardiac Rehabilitation (APBCRE) program for patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), and to assess the validity of the oxygen uptake efficiency slope (OUES) as a measure of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation outcomes.

pmc-13407630.creator: Heeyeon Son, Springer Cary, Sungsil Hong, Jung Woo Han, Cecile Lengacher, Sharron L. Docherty

pmc-13431499.title: Topological Stability and Transcritical Bifurcations in a Target-Cell-Limited Model of HBV-HDV Viral Interference
pmc-13431499.creator: Menachem Lachiany
pmc-13431499.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). While minimalist kinetic models effectively capture the acute inverse coupling between Hepatitis B (HBV) and Hepatitis Delta (HDV), they often fail to account for the asymptotic stability and long-term viral plateaus observed during clinical therapy. In this work, we present an expanded compartmental framework integrating the non-linear dynamics of susceptible (S) and infected (I) hepatocyte populations, explicitly incorporating the satellite nature of HDV.

pmc-13461083.title: Effects of prophylactic tranexamic acid on bleeding during transbronchial lung biopsy: a double-blind, randomized controlled trial
pmc-13461083.creator: Marzieh Rostami, Ali Dabbagh, Alireza JolousJamshidi, Alireza Shakeri, Kamal Fani, Marzie Shahrabi, Hamidreza Samadpour, Seyed Mohammad Seyed-Alshohadaei, Maede Karimian
pmc-13461083.description: Background:This randomized controlled trial evaluated the efficacy of tranexamic acid in preventing bleeding in patients undergoing transbronchial lung biopsy.Materials and methods:This study was a double-blind, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial. Adult patients referred for flexible bronchoscopy with a planned transbronchial lung biopsy during 2024 were included in the current study.

pmc-13549293.title: Radiographers’ Experiences of Clinical Handover in Diagnostic Imaging: A Qualitative Study of Communication, Safety, and Organizational Influences
pmc-13549293.creator: Chandra Rekha Makanjee, Jasjeet Kaur, Robin Hart
pmc-13549293.description: BackgroundHandover in diagnostic medical imaging (DMI) is a critical process involving the transfer of professional responsibility, clinical information, and patient accountability between healthcare practitioners, supported by the communication practices that enable this information exchange. Although handover is widely recognized as essential to patient safety in broader healthcare, the specific experiences and perspectives of radiographers within DMI encounters remain insufficiently explored.
